record.field:
3-step playbook for patients who submit the "Book a Consultation" form on the hospital website.
Step 1 (immediate): Call to understand which department they need, confirm insurance / self-pay, and check if appointment is urgent. Step 2 (immediate): Assign to Online Enquiries Team for ongoing ownership. Step 3 (2 days later): Follow-up call to confirm booking and answer questions.
Qualification call — understand department and insurance
Call patient — qualify department need and confirm insurance / payment method

ol.li: Introduce yourself and confirm this is a good time to talk.
Ask what type of consultation they need (e.g. cardiology, orthopaedics, general).
Confirm whether they are using health insurance or self-pay.
Check urgency — are they in pain now or planning ahead?
Offer available appointment slots or book a callback with the specialist team.
Log outcome in the lead notes before hanging up.

record.field: Follow-up call — confirm booking (2 days later)
Follow-up — confirm appointment booking and answer any remaining questions

ol.li: Confirm the patient booked their appointment (if so, close this lead as Won).
If not booked: ask what is holding them back and offer alternatives.
If they chose another provider: log as Lost with reason for future analysis.
If still deciding: schedule another follow-up in 5 days.

record.field: Single-step high-priority playbook for paid Cardiology Ads leads. These leads are actively searching for cardiac care right now. Target: call within 1 hour. The Cardiology Business Team owns these leads.
HIGH PRIORITY — Call within 1 hour (Cardiology Ads lead)
HIGH PRIORITY — Cardiology Ads lead. Call within 1 hour.

field.name: activity_note
field.p: This is a paid Cardiology Ads lead — call immediately. Speed is the biggest conversion factor for paid-search patients.

ol.li: Introduce yourself from the Cardiology department.
Ask what cardiac symptom or concern brought them to search today.
Assess urgency — chest pain, palpitations, or routine ECG check?
If urgent: connect directly to triage nurse or emergency line.
If routine: offer a same-week or next-day specialist appointment.
Confirm insurance / payment and book the slot before hanging up.

p.em: If no answer: leave a brief voicemail mentioning the hospital name, then schedule a callback activity for 3 hours later.

record.field: [HOSP] Health and Wellness Fair — Event Follow-Up

2-step playbook for contacts collected at the Health and Wellness Fair 2026. Sales reps launch this manually from the CRM lead form after entering the contact. Step 1: call the same day to re-establish rapport while the event is fresh. Step 2: assign to Field Sales Team for long-term ownership.
Call today — while the event is fresh in their memory
Health fair follow-up call — re-establish rapport, confirm interest

field.name: activity_note
field.p: Context: You met this person at the Health and Wellness Fair.

ol.li: Remind them where you met and what you discussed at the booth.
Ask if they had a chance to review any materials you shared.
For corporate contacts (HR Managers): offer a free group health screening package — ask how many employees.
For individuals: ask which health concern they are most interested in addressing.
Agree on a next step (appointment, proposal, or another call).

record.field: 2-step low-pressure playbook for exploratory leads from the hospital blog. These visitors are researching, not yet ready to book. Step 1: send a warm welcome email immediately (no sales pressure). Step 2: gentle follow-up call the next day to answer questions. Routes to Marketing / Nurture team until they warm up. Requires a configured outgoing mail server for Step 1.
Send welcome email (immediate — no sales pressure)
Gentle follow-up call (next day — answer questions, no pressure)
Organic blog lead — low-pressure call, answer questions, no hard sell

field.name: activity_note
field.p: Approach: This person is researching, not ready to commit yet. Be helpful, not pushy.

ol.li: Reference the welcome email you sent yesterday.
Ask what health topic they were reading about on the blog.
Answer any questions about services, costs, or what to expect at a consultation.
If interest is strong: offer a free 15-minute phone consultation with a specialist.
If still exploring: offer to send relevant articles or a service brochure via email.
Do NOT pressure them to book — that will lose the relationship.

record.field: 2-step playbook for patient referrals received from other doctors or clinics. Referrals are pre-qualified — the priority is fast specialist matching. Step 1: call the referring doctor (not the patient) to clarify diagnosis, urgency, and what specialist they recommend. Step 2: assign to Medical Liaison Team who coordinates specialist booking. Launch this manually from the lead form after logging the referral.
Call referring doctor — confirm diagnosis, urgency, specialist needed
Call referring doctor — confirm patient details, urgency level, and specialist recommendation

field.name: activity_note

p.strong: Call the referring doctor (Dr. / Clinic in the lead's Company field), not the patient directly.

ol.li: Confirm patient name, age, and contact number.
What is the primary diagnosis or concern being referred for?
Is this urgent (days) or routine (weeks)?
Which specialist or department do you recommend?
Are there any existing test results or imaging we should receive?
Should the patient contact you before coming in, or go directly to us?

field.p: Log all details as a note on this lead before closing the activity.

record.field: Assign to Medical Liaison Team for specialist matching
